extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of psychology/psychoanalysis and humor theory
extracted.subtask_description: Theoretical criteria for creating and analysing wit, jokes, the naive, and the comic from a Freudian/psychoanalytic perspective, focusing on techniques (word-play, displacement, irony), social conditions, and psychical mechanisms (inhibition, unconscious selection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Displacement as a technique
rubrics_metrics.description: The dream-work and wit solve the task of inhibition by displacements — substituting remote ideas for objectionable ones so they can pass the censor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displacements include deviations from the trend of thought and all forms of indirect expression; in wit these occur but usually within the limits prescribed for conscious thought. Examples: deviation of trend of thought used as a source of pleasure; displacements facilitate tendency-wit when overcoming multiple inhibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect representation / allusion / substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use substitution of an offensive element by an apparently indifferent one (allusion), symbols, comparisons, or trifles to hint at the forbidden thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indirect expressions make the reference to the original thought findable yet disguised. Dream-work exaggerates their use; wit employs them but restricts their application so the third person can decipher them (jest vs dream exaggeration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outer associations vs inner associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Substituting inner associations (similarity, causal connection) with outer associations (simultaneity, contiguity in space, assonance) is characteristic of dream-work and can appear in wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outer associations are particularly conspicuous in dream-work; in wit they may be used sparingly as sources of word-play or contiguous associations (e.g., punning by sound similarity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity and multiplicity of thought-relations (double-sidedness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit exploits the ambiguity of words and multiplicity of thought relations to retain the play (sense in nonsense) while restricting its appearance to admissible contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'double-sidedness' — emphasizing 'sense in nonsense' — is central to wit: it permits play with words without destroying intelligibility. Authors who find 'sense in nonsense' approach the understanding of wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of play without compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit does not make compromises like the dream; it retains the play or nonsense unaltered but selects contexts where such play is simultaneously admissible (a jest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because wit must be social/intelligible, it restricts displacement and disguise to what a third person can decipher. The result is a deliberate balancing act: keep play intact but choose moments where it passes as admissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation through the opposite / irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the opposite (saying one thing to mean the reverse) is a powerful wit-technique closely allied to the comic; irony imparts the opposite of what is intended while signalling the reversal by inflection, gesture, or style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irony is applicable only where the hearer is prepared to hear the reverse and thus inclined to contradict; it is particularly liable to misunderstanding. Psychologically, it produces comic pleasure by causing preparations for contradiction that prove unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonsense and absurdity as deliberate devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonsense and absurdity in dreams and wit are not accidental shufflings but are purposely admitted to express scorn or judgment (e.g., 'It's pure nonsense').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In wit, nonsense can heighten psychic expenditure in the hearer and thus increase laughter; nonsense can also be an end in itself (reviving pleasure in nonsense). Caricature, exaggeration, parody, and travesty can produce 'comical nonsense' without invoking unconscious processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social requirement: intelligibility to the third person
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is intensely social and often requires a third person; it must bind itself to the condition of intelligibility and therefore limit the extent of condensation/displacement to what the third person can decipher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because wit's pleasurable process involves another's comprehension, techniques that make material undecipherable (as in dream-work) are curtailed. Wit frequently involves three persons in the psychic process; the third person completes the pleasure-bearing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between dream-technique and wit-technique
rubrics_metrics.description: While both use similar means (displacement, indirect representation), dream-work applies them without regard for intelligibility and social constraints, whereas wit restricts their use to what remains intelligible and admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dreams may invert elements or represent opposites without regard to comprehension; wit must keep disguise within decipherable bounds so the social audience can share the pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types/stages of wit (jest, harmless wit, tendency-wit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different forms of wit have distinct origins and requirements: the jest (originates in happy mood, uses wit-techniques and lowers psychic energy), harmless wit (expresses a valuable thought and may require personal adaptation), and tendency-wit (serves unconscious tendencies and often requires unconscious remodeling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jest benefits from a lowered psychic static (happy mood); harmless wit relies on the producer's readiness to express foreconscious material; tendency-wit may need the unconscious to draw foreconscious thought down for remodeling (common in 'cynical' witticisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lowering of foreconscious occupation energy / unconscious selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of the exact form of expression that yields word-pleasure is not made by conscious attention; it is favored when the occupation energy of the foreconscious thought is lowered to the unconscious, where associative paths are treated equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unconscious provides more favorable conditions for selecting word-play and multiple associations; raising the unconscious influence can assist in finding the felicitous form that produces the gain in word-pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-pleasure as a kernel and removal/release pleasure as shell
rubrics_metrics.description: The affective determination of wit combines a kernel of word-pleasure or nonsense-pleasure with a surrounding pleasure due to removal or release of inhibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective wit must produce both components: the immediate delight of the word-play (kernel) and the secondary pleasure from economizing or discharging inhibition energy (shell).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of mood and personal aptitude
rubrics_metrics.description: A happy mood lowers psychic energy and facilitates jest-making; aptitude for joking independent of mood exists but is rarer and linked to personal adaptation that allows foreconscious thoughts to sink momentarily into the unconscious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most people make jests when happy; a few individuals can produce wit independently of mood, and neurotic persons may be especially fitted for wit when strong unconscious tendencies are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allusion and displacement to overcome dual inhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency-wit that faces two kinds of inhibitions (opposed to itself and to its tendency) frequently uses allusion and displacement to facilitate overcoming these inhibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allusion/displacement serve to circumvent conscious objections by pointing indirectly to the forbidden thought, allowing the witticism to be articulated where a direct statement would be suppressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naive as a distinct species with social-recognition condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The naive arises when the producing person lacks inhibitions; the hearer must recognize that the producer has no inhibition to call the utterance naive rather than obscene or improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naive speech uses the same wording/techniques as wit but without intention; the pleasure depends on the hearer imagining the producer's psychic state and economizing expenditure by comparison, discharging inhibition-energy through laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure from economized expenditure / comparison mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Comic pleasure (especially in the naive) arises from an economy of expenditure when one puts oneself into the psychic process of the producing person and compares it with one's own — saved inhibition expenditure is discharged as laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism differs from explanations that attribute comic pleasure to oscillation of attention; it emphasizes saved work (inhibition energy) through psychological contrast as the source of pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naive vs wit: source of pleasure differs by assumed intention
rubrics_metrics.description: What distinguishes naive from wit is not wording or technique but whether the speaker intended to be witty; if the speaker intended an earnest conclusion based on ignorance, the result is naive rather than wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For analysts/creators: ensure the audience's perception of intention lines up with the intended category (naive vs witty)—misalignment changes the affective response (laughter vs indignation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic as broader category found primarily in persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The comical appears first in human persons — their movements, shapes, actions, character traits — and only later by transference in objects or situations (via personification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing the comic, focus on person-centered contrasts and psychical peculiarity; personification of objects can evoke the comic but is derivative of the person-based source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decipherability constraint on disfigurement/condensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any disfigurement (condensation, displacement) used by wit must be limited so that it remains decipherable by the intelligence of the third person; otherwise the social function (shared pleasure) fails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting or evaluating a witticism, balance the degree of disguise against the likely interpretive ability of the audience; dream-level disfigurements would be incomprehensible and therefore non-functional in wit.
